messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER → Severity P1 — Elevated 5xx/504 rate observed on gateway egress to aws-s3-prod (us-west-2). 5xx rate ~18% over 5m. Paging: @maria

maria: I'm oncall. pulling logs and traces now. can someone drop the top corrids we're seeing?

jon: dumping a quick tail from ingress logs, looks like a cluster of 504s with upstream reset. sample corrids: c0rr-9f7a, c0rr-a12b, c0rr-44ff, c0rr-8b2c

jon: log snippet:

```
2026-02-13T20:01:03Z gateway svc=request id=c0rr-9f7a upstream=proxy-s3-1 code=504 msg="upstream timeout: read reset"
2026-02-13T20:01:04Z gateway svc=request id=c0rr-a12b upstream=proxy-s3-1 code=502 msg="upstream connection reset by peer"
2026-02-13T20:01:07Z gateway svc=request id=c0rr-44ff upstream=proxy-s3-2 code=504 msg="read timeout after 15s"
```
\nmaria: thanks. jon, can you attach the full 10m bucket? upload to the incident artifacts channel and paste link.

jon: uploaded -> https://files.redwood.test/incidents/1755555555/logs.tar.gz (note: huge jsonl ~ 12MB, includes request/response headers)

devin: I see a sudden spike in retry patterns from client-side SDKs around 20:00Z — retries clustered 20:00:10 → 20:01:10. looks like a concurrent retry amplification.

lisa: deploy-bot shows no code deploys in the last 45m. config push? nothing listed either.

raj: tracing shows backend proxy to s3-upload-proxy reporting increased RTOs and 429s in a short burst, then connection resets. Hypothesis: upstream rate-limited, causing retries to pile up and overwhelm connection pools.

maria: hypothesis noted: upstream (s3-proxy) rate-limited -> client retries -> connection pool exhaustion -> gateway 5xx/504. we need quick mitigation: reduce downstream retries and fallback route.

eng-runtime: immediate mitigations we can enact now:
- enable circuit-breaker on egress path for s3-upload-proxy (fail fast)
- route 20% of traffic to s3-us-east-1 fallback host for uploads
- temporarily raise backend timeouts to avoid premature retry storms (short-term only)

maria: doing the circuit-breaker + fallback route now. will also throttle our internal concurrent uploader to 50% for 10m.

customer-success: heads-up — we're seeing user reports for upload failures (multi-tenant). flagging high-value customers for follow-up.

jon: circuit-breaker config applied at 20:03:12Z (threshold=5s, consecutive-errors=5). routing rule rollout started 20:04:05Z to 20% of egress.

devin: telemetry after change: 20:06Z 5xx rate dropped to 6% over 2m, latency stabilized. initial mitigation working.

maria: good. next steps for in-incident RCA:
- collect full kvlogs + traces for corrids above (jon)
- correlate client retry spikes to SDK version and client-hosts (devin)
- check upstream s3-upload-proxy scaling / throttles (raj)
- customer impact list for CS (customer-success)
- create timeline + draft RCA (maria)

jon: uploaded kvlogs & trace bundles -> https://files.redwood.test/incidents/1755555555/kvlogs_traces.tar.gz (contains top corrids).

raj: early look at upstream metrics shows 429 bursts and a backend autoscaler flapping because of a mis-sized connection pool (we'll dig deeper in postmortem).

maria: tagging this thread as active RCA. please keep replies on-thread and add any new corrids. I'm going to build the minute-by-minute timeline using jon's logs and the tracer.

devin: adding note — proposing a follow-up fix: backpressure token bucket at gateway + stricter client SDK retry jitter to avoid synchronized retry waves.

customer-success: notified impacted customers at 20:15Z, offering prioritized retries and support.

maria: final sync for the incident: mitigation held, 5xx baseline restored at 20:10Z. we'll keep fallback route until root cause patch. action items assigned in #incidents-runbook. prepping RCA doc now. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED? (manual review required)
